sources.title: McEvedy & Jones, Atlas of World Population History (population anchors)

uncertainties: Verification searches were unavailable this session (proxy limits); all assignments drawn from standard scholarship (Wikipedia-level consensus, McEvedy & Jones anchors). Facts I would re-verify first: exact 476 holders of Pannonia/Savia, Vandal control of Tripolitania in 440 vs 442 treaty, and the 591 Byzantine-Persian partition line in Iberia/Armenia.

476 Pannonia: brief assigns Ostrogoths, but the Amal Goths had largely moved to the Balkans by 473; I gave them CRO/BOS (Savia) and Gepids the Tisza core (HUN/TRN/SVK/WLC). Heruli (Morava) and Sciri omitted as too fine-grained.
SVK 476-527 given to Gepids as a simplification; in reality Heruli then pre-Italian Lombards held the Morava-Slovakia belt.
Lombards appear from 540 as tribal with founded=488 (Rugiland/Danube), switching to canonical founded=568 as the Italian kingdom from 580 - mirrors the franks 257->481 treatment.
franks founded shifts 257 (tribal, per era05) to 481 (Clovis, canonical) at the 500 slice; byzantium/west_rome keep founded=-509 with continuity notes per the registry (era07 uses 395 for byzantium).

CRM (Crimea): follows era05's 395 choice of Hunnic control until 476; Byzantine from 500 (Justinian refortifies Cherson/Bosporus). In reality Cherson stayed Roman throughout; Crimean Goths are noted only in text.

Mauro-Roman kingdoms (Altava, Aures) carried under id berber_tribes (founded 477) so the entity joins era07's berber_tribes seamlessly; NUM stays Byzantine 540-600 and passes to Berbers only in era07's 620 slice.
Ghassanids carried under id arabs_early ('Ghassanid Arabs' 527-580, renamed 'Arab tribes' at 600 after Maurice broke the phylarchate in 584) to join era07's arabs_early without an id change.
OCC (Languedoc & Toulouse) stays Visigothic after Vouille 507 because Septimania (Narbonne) dominated the region's coast; Toulouse itself was Frankish - matches era07's choice.
Baleares (BAL) kept Vandal 476-527, Byzantine from 540; Malta assumed to follow Sicily's holder (Odoacer/Ostrogoths, then Byzantium from 535) - Vandal tenure there is debated.
600 Caucasus reflects the 591 treaty: ARM and GEO to Byzantium; era07's 620 slice returns both to Persia during the great war - the flip is intentional.

Slavic expansion timeline: Bohemia 565, Vistula 565-580, Elbe (BRA) and East-Slavic BLR/RUS_S by 600; western-Balkan CRO/BOS/SRB shown Slavic at 600 per brief, though mass settlement is usually dated after 602 - Byzantium lists them as contested claims.

Population: brief's 'Italy 5M->3M' and plague losses encoded via byzantium 28M (540 peak) -> 19M (565) -> 14M (600) and Frankish/British declines; individual kingdom figures interpolate McEvedy & Jones and are +/-30%.
SCO_S relabelled picts->britons at 410 (era05 gave the Lowlands to Picts at 395): the Old North (Gododdin, Strathclyde) was Brittonic; the shift is a correction, not a conquest.
